strengths: Addresses genuine gap: First large-scale RGB-Thermal visual grounding benchmark for complex real-world scenarios with clear motivation for safety-critical applications

Comprehensive benchmark design: 40K images with multi-level annotations (13 scene types, 4 lighting/weather conditions), significantly higher proportions of challenging samples (57.7% small objects, 23.1% low-light), and longer queries (14.24 words)

Rigorous data construction pipeline: Careful three-stage filtering (visibility/scale, cross-modality alignment, category balance), LVLM-based annotation with human verification, and statistical validation of annotation quality
Unified RGBT-VG framework: Enables fair comparison by systematizing training, preprocessing, and evaluation across RGB-only, TIR-only, and RGB+TIR baselines on seven representative methods

Thorough experimental evaluation: 60+ configurations, specialized test splits (TestA/B/C), extensive fine-grained analysis across 25+ subsets (scenes, weather, illumination, sizes, occlusion), consistent method rankings across datasets, and effective ablations demonstrating component contributions

Strong empirical results: RGBT-VGNet achieves superior performance in challenging scenarios (nighttime: 67.19% vs 66.09%, small objects: 52.22% vs 51.16%), particularly benefiting from RGB-TIR fusion in adverse conditions
Reproducibility commitment: Plans to release benchmark data, framework codes, model implementations, and evaluation toolkits to enable community adoption and future research

High-quality presentation: Well-organized paper with informative visualizations, comprehensive 30-page appendix containing detailed per-scene/weather/illumination results, qualitative comparisons, and ablations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in baseline method: AMA is essentially asymmetric LoRA (straightforward adaptation of existing technique), and LAVS uses standard cross-attention—the true contribution is the benchmark, not algorithmic innovation; no comparison to alternative modality adaptation strategies

Annotation quality verification gaps: Proportion of manually verified instances not specified, no inter-annotator agreement metrics (Cohen's kappa, Fleiss' kappa) provided, and LVLM annotation dependency creates potential for systematic biases not fully explored

Data selection bias: Selecting largest instance per image may bias toward salient objects; long-tail category filtering reduces diversity; imbalanced scene distribution (Urban 13K vs Waterfront 807 instances) not thoroughly discussed

Insufficient modality complementarity analysis: Limited mechanistic understanding of when/why RGB+TIR helps; missing attention visualizations showing modality contributions; marginal improvements in well-lit conditions lack significance analysis; no exploration of failure modes where fusion hurts performance

Experimental limitations: Missing result indicators ('-' entries in Tables 4-5 unexplained), train/test splits follow source dataset boundaries rather than random partitioning (potential systematic bias), only Acc@0.5 metric used (Acc@0.7 would strengthen claims), zero-shot evaluation de-emphasized as expected yet still heavily presented

Insufficient AMA design justification: Limited theoretical or empirical justification for asymmetric rank selection (rv ≤ rt); no ablation comparing to symmetric LoRA or exploring rank sensitivity; hierarchical design mentioned but not detailed or ablated separately

Application-specific scope limitations: Benchmark heavily weighted toward outdoor urban/rural scenes from vehicle detection datasets; limited indoor scenarios; generalization to other domains unexplored; results may not transfer to alternative RGB-TIR collection modalities or sensor types

Missing critical analyses: No cross-dataset transfer evaluation (train on RefFLIR → test on RefM3FD); no backward compatibility assessment on existing RGB-only benchmarks; limited exploration of TIR failure modes (reflective surfaces, thermal homogeneity); insufficient justification for why LAVS outperforms simpler fusion strategies
